name: Cloudroot Pass
description: The path leaves the pilgrim road and climbs a spine of black stone. Here the world grows thin: the clouds below are a white sea, and above, a single peak pierces heaven like a brushstroke of ink. A small guardhouse of weather-silvered wood leans against the cliff. Prayer flags, half-shredded, crack in the wind — the sound is like distant fighting.
first_visit_text: You step above the cloud line for the first time. The air is thinner here, and older. Every breath tastes of iron and high wind. A voice from the guardhouse calls, without hurry: 'Few come this far with a full dantian, fewer with a full heart. Show me both, or show me the way down.'

name: Hanging Terraces of Jadestep
description: Stepped platforms cling to the cliff like broken stairs for a fallen giant. Cracked flagstones still bear the worn crane-and-peak crest of the Jadestep Sect, who died out four hundred years ago. Green lichen grows where disciples once knelt. Wind-sung prayer bells, long cracked, give off a sound like weeping glass whenever the gale turns.

name: Thunderhead Ridge
description: A knife-thin ridge walks between two abysses. On either hand the clouds boil — slate-dark, fat with unspent lightning. The stone itself hums, and the hair along your forearms stands up as if greeting an old teacher. Every few breaths, thunder cracks a quarter-mile below, pale blue fire walking sideways through cloud.
first_visit_text: A bolt of lightning leaps up from below and dies in the air a hand's span from your face. You taste copper. Whatever comes next, it will remember this ridge as the place it began.

name: The Skyweaver's Cloister
description: A hermitage of cedar and grey stone, tucked into a lee of the cliff where the wind cannot find it. An iron teapot sits on a cold brazier; a single worn cushion faces the opening. The air here is pulled taut and quiet, as if the room itself were listening. On the far wall, nine sword-scars are cut in a line — and, beside them, a tenth, halfway finished.
first_visit_text: As you cross the threshold a voice — dry, kind, tired — says from behind you: 'So. Another student, come to ask a dead man for lessons. Sit. The tea has been waiting longer than you have been alive.'

name: Cragspine Shrine
description: A natural altar of wind-scoured stone, set atop a spur of rock that juts out over a mile of empty air. Here the sky itself feels close enough to reach into. Nine old incense stubs stand in a ring around a pale crystal that was never carved — only grown. The qi here is layered, like folded silk: breathe in and the meridians widen without your asking.

name: Spirit-Gale Plateau
description: The ridge opens at last onto a white plateau of bleached stone. Wind strong enough to push a man to his knees scours every direction at once, and the clouds split around the summit like a river parting at a rock. At the far end, the true Sky-Spire rises — a single black needle of peak no mortal hand has ever climbed. Something is waiting here; you have known it was waiting since Cloudroot.
first_visit_text: The wind dies for a single breath — the gale, which has not stopped since Cloudroot, simply ceases. In that silence, four yellow eyes open in the middle distance. The plateau, you understand, was never empty.
